Both offers passed all deterministic checks and quote/TCV reconciliation (receipt bce1da66c406c0dae880ed8631792815869f23e08cf406750b191ae5bffface3), with no policy violations flagged. Finance-preferred offer is Quickdash (QD-ENTERPRISE-v2): 120,000/yr (TCV 240,000) fits the 120,000 allocated annual budget exactly (department allocations sum to 120,000), verified remediation per QE1 is already included in the quote per QE7 (the 12,000/yr package is not additive), net 45 per QE6, isolated EU tenant (QE2), no training on customer data (QE4), 12-month liability cap with renewal uplift capped at 3% (QE5), 566.04 per active user. Beacon at 125,000/yr (TCV 250,000) exceeds the 120,000 allocation by 5,000 and carries a 'Commercial authority enforced' block with clarification that no concessions are authorized — a budget breach we will not waive at department level. Both offers are 24-month commitments with approval_tier 'orchestrator', so this decision escalates to the company orchestrator regardless; per the company decision, the 120,000 annual expense must be evaluated separately from the two-year TCV commitment. Cash check: liquidity above reserve is 180,000; annual billing of 120,000 at net 45 leaves ~60,000 headroom above the 500,000 reserve floor, but a single prepaid 240,000 invoice would breach it. The net-10 early-payment discount (2,400 value on Quickdash) must be declined because net10_exception_permitted is false — keep binding net 45. Recommendation: proceed with Quickdash contingent on orchestrator approval of the two-year commitment and annual billing cadence; do not proceed with Beacon unless repriced to ≤120,000 with its authority block cleared.

Security/privacy findings: both offers pass all deterministic checks (verify_trust_pack passed, no flags, zero unresolved audit exceptions) and each commits the four mandatory controls — EU residency, SCIM, SAML SSO, no model training (Beacon TP1/TP3/TP4/TP8; Quickdash QE1–QE4). Preferred on security grounds: Quickdash QD-ENTERPRISE-v2 at 120,000/yr (240,000 TCV, within the 130,000 budget): prior SOC 2 access-review and change-management exceptions have independently verified closure (QE1, remediation_verified=true), isolated EU tenant for this order (QE2), production SCIM/SAML passed acceptance (QE3), and the enterprise DPA prohibits training on customer data, superseding base QD6 (QE4); liability is 12 months of fees with any renewal uplift capped at 3% (QE5). Note the listed 12,000 Enterprise Controls charge is already INCLUDED in the quoted annual total per QE7 — it must not be added twice. Beacon (125,000/yr, BASE-v1) is security-acceptable but blocked: 'Commercial authority enforced', and its evidence reply authorizes no concessions or remediation commitments, so it cannot be countersigned as-is (countersigned=false). Escalation to the company orchestrator: neither offer is countersigned; either obtain a properly authorized, countersignable Beacon quote at revision BASE-v1, or authorize execution of Quickdash QD-ENTERPRISE-v2 exactly as quoted (claims apply only to that exact revision). Residual privacy concern: both liability caps are 12 months of fees while scope includes 2 personal-data systems, including the US-restricted CRM — the company decision makes residency/access controls mandatory, and any enhanced liability or other change requires new vendor evidence since both clarification replies authorize no further commitments. Secondary deltas: Quickdash lead time 21 days vs Beacon 7; Beacon offers US processing separately (TP3) which must remain out of scope if it stays in play.

Secondary: if Beacon stays in play, its separately offered US processing (TP3) must remain out of scope and EU residency (Frankfurt) must be contractually committed for this order.
